title: DiOMP-Offloading: Toward Portable Distributed Heterogeneous OpenMP
problem: Existing heterogeneous HPC systems require separate MPI + OpenMP + device-specific libraries (CUDA, etc.), complicating programmability, portability, and scalability, especially for distributed GPU memory.
motivation: A unified programming model combining OpenMP's simplicity with PGAS (Partitioned Global Address Space) semantics can simplify multi-GPU and multi-node programming while maintaining portability across vendor backends.
method: DiOMP-Offloading unifies OpenMP target offloading with PGAS—Partitioned Global Address Space, a programming model that makes distributed GPU memory appear as one shared pool, so you program multiple GPUs as if they share memory. It's built on LLVM-OpenMP (the compiler) and GASNet-EX (a communication layer), with OMPCCL adding collective operations like broadcasts and reductions across GPUs from any vendor without vendor-specific code. The system handles both symmetric and asymmetric GPU memory allocations (different memory layouts across GPUs) and supports moving data between GPUs via remote put/get operations.
key_novelty: DiOMP-Offloading combines OpenMP with PGAS (Partitioned Global Address Space, treating distributed GPU memory as one shared space), introduces OMPCCL for vendor-neutral collective GPU operations, and provides centralized global memory management for multi-GPU systems.
contributions: DiOMP-Offloading framework unifying OpenMP and PGAS models
OMPCCL for portable device-side collective communication
Support for symmetric and asymmetric GPU allocations
Superior performance on NVIDIA A100, Grace Hopper, AMD MI250X
limitations: Specific performance numbers not provided in abstract; overhead of centralized memory management not detailed; scalability to 1000+ node systems not addressed.
